content: 1. Cases of anaphylaxis and anaphylactic shock, including fatal outcomes, have been reported following either initial exposure or re-exposure to Synagis (palivizumab). 2. Other acute hypersensitivity reactions, which may be severe, have also been observed after initial exposure or re-exposure to Synagis. 3. Symptoms of hypersensitivity reactions may include urticaria (hives), pruritus (itching), angioedema (swelling), dyspnea (difficulty breathing), respiratory failure, cyanosis (bluish discoloration of the skin), hypotonia (reduced muscle tone), hypotension (low blood pressure), and unresponsiveness. 4. The relationship between these hypersensitivity reactions and the development of antibodies to Synagis is currently unknown. 5. If a significant hypersensitivity reaction occurs during the use of Synagis, its administration should be permanently discontinued. 6. In cases of severe hypersensitivity reactions, appropriate medical treatment (e.g., epinephrine) and supportive care should be provided as necessary. 7. If a mild hypersensitivity reaction occurs, clinical judgment should be exercised to determine whether cautious re-administration of Synagis is appropriate. 8. Synagis is intended for intramuscular use only. 9. As with any intramuscular injection, Synagis should be administered with caution in children who have thrombocytopenia (low platelet count) or any coagulation disorder. 10. Palivizumab may interfere with immunological-based diagnostic tests, such as certain antigen detection assays. 11. Additionally, palivizumab inhibits viral replication in cell culture, which may interfere with viral culture assays. 12. Palivizumab does not interfere with reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)-based assays. 13. Interference with diagnostic assays could result in false-negative test results. 14. Therefore, diagnostic test results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings to guide medical decisions. 15. The safety and efficacy of Synagis have not been established for the treatment of active disease. 16. The single-dose vial of Synagis does not contain a preservative. 17. Synagis should be administered immediately after the dose is withdrawn from the vial. 18. The vial should not be re-entered after the initial withdrawal. 19. Any unused portion of the medication should be discarded.
